description:
tests/types_test.rs lines 791-1254 introduce a `mod jscalendar_roundtrip` containing 11 round-trip tests that prove every Option<serde_json::Value>-typed field on Task / TaskList can be decoded into the corresponding typed sub-type from jmap-jscalendar-types and re-encoded byte-equivalently.

This is the test-discipline that the sloppy-Value pattern requires: callers are told "use serde_json::from_value::<Location>(...)" — and this test suite proves that contract holds for each of the 11 fields, with hand-written JSON fixtures sourced from RFC 8984 §4.x and §6.x (each citing the section in a per-test comment).

The test fixtures use independent oracles (RFC 8984 §6.2, §6.8, §6.9, §6.10 verbatim examples), not values derived from the code under test. The pattern is documented in a 25-line module-level comment with the five-step recipe (build, deserialize, extract, typed-decode, byte-equal re-encode).

What a future contributor or commenter might suggest:
  - "fold these tests together using a macro" — defend by pointing at the per-RFC-section comments; the readability of the per-field test outweighs the macro's line savings.
  - "remove this test, the sloppy fields are just Value, what is there to test" — defend by pointing at the consumer contract: any future change that breaks the typed-decode path is a silent API break.

Do not let anyone consolidate, parameterize, or weaken these tests. They are the verification that the "hybrid sloppy-value pattern" (PLAN.md §1-§8 in the calendars sibling) actually works for tasks.
title: JSCalendar sloppy-Value round-trip test suite (11 tests in jscalendar_roundtrip module)
